Rashi on Gittin 49b:11:1.english: For the sake of favor - so that men will find favor in the eyes of women and [the women] will marry them:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:14:1.english: From whom - [does the Gemara] say [this regarding] all these [cases] of the Mishnah:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:14:2.hebrew: אילימא מיתמי - נזקין היכא דמית מזיק וגבי מיתמי, מי גבי מעידית? הא תנן: "אין נפרעים מנכסי יתומים אלא מזיבורית":
Rashi on Gittin 49b:14:2.english: If we say from the orphans - [Regarding] damages, where the damager died and [the injured party] collects from the orphans, does he collect from superior-quality land? Behold, we learned [in a Mishnah]: "One collects from the property of orphans only from inferior-quality land":

Rashi on Gittin 49b:15:1.hebrew: כגון שנעשה ערב כו' - לעולם כתובה מיניה דידיה בבינונית, וכולה מתני' בערב קמיירי: שנעשה ערב לבנו לנזקו ולהלואתו ולכתובת אשתו, לפורעה בשבילו אם לא יפרעה; ולא פרעה ומת, ואתו וגבו מן הערב. והכא ודאי, אע"ג דלאו מיתמי גביא, לא מגבינן לה אלא מזיבורית, דהאי כי דיניה והאי כי דיניה:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:15:1.english: Where he became a guarantor, etc. - In fact, a ketubah [collected] from [the husband] himself is [collected] from medium-quality land, and the entire Mishnah is speaking of a guarantor: where he became a guarantor for his son — for his damages, for his loan, and for his wife's ketubah — to pay it on his behalf if he does not pay it; and he did not pay it and died, and they came and collected from the guarantor. And here certainly, even though she is not collecting from orphans, we only allow her to collect from inferior-quality land, because each one [collects] according to his respective law.

Rashi on Gittin 49b:16:1.hebrew: נזקין וחוב - דדינייהו ליפרע נמי מחיים של בן, תביעתן אינה באה כצועקים על היתומים; לפיכך כשנפרעים מן הערב, נפרעים ממנו כדין שהיו נפרעים מן הבן אם היה בחיים והיו לו נכסים:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:16:1.english: Injured parties and a debt - Since their law is also to collect during the lifetime of the son, their claim does not come like those crying out against orphans; therefore, when they collect from the guarantor, they collect from him according to the law [by which] they would collect from the son if he were alive and had property:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:16:2.english: From whom does she collect - [meaning,] if the son had property:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:17:1.hebrew: לא משתעבד - לפרוע, דהכי פסקינן הלכתא לקמן בסמוך:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:17:1.english: Does not become obligated - to pay, for so we rule the halakha shortly below:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:17:2.hebrew: בקבלן - שנעשה עליה קבלן, שהתפיסה בנו מטלטלין לכתובתה, והיא מסרתן לידו בתורת קבלנות, והחזירתן לבנו:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:17:2.english: With an unconditional guarantor - who became an unconditional guarantor for her [marriage contract], in that his son gave her possession of movable property for her marriage contract, and she handed them over to him [the father] in the capacity of an unconditional guarantor, and returned them to his son:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:18:1.hebrew: הניחא למ"ד - בב"ב, בגט פשוט:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:18:1.english: This works out well according to the one who says - in Bava Batra, in [the chapter entitled] Get Pashut:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:18:2.hebrew: אית ליה נכסי ללוה - בשעת הלואה, דאיכא למימר עלייהו סמיך הערב הזה, וגמר ושעבד נפשיה:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:18:2.english: [If] the borrower has property - at the time of the loan, for one can say [that] this guarantor relies upon it, and [therefore] resolves and obligates himself:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:18:3.hebrew: משתעבד - ואם שטפו נהר אחרי כן, נפרעין מן הערב:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:18:3.english: [He] becomes obligated - And if a river swept [his property] away afterward, they collect from the guarantor:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:18:4.hebrew: מאי איכא למימר - הא ודאי לית ליה נכסים לאותו הבן, דאי הוו ליה נכסים — לא היו פורעים מן הערב, דתנן: המלוה את חבירו ע"י ערב, לא יפרע מן הערב (תחילה), ומוקמינן: לא יתבע מן הערב תחילה:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:18:4.english: What is there to say - Surely that son has no property, for if he had property, they would not collect from the guarantor, as we learned [in a Mishnah]: "One who lends [money] to his fellow through a guarantor may not collect from the guarantor (first)," and we establish [that this means]: he may not demand [payment] from the guarantor first:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:19:1.english: Where [there] were - properties [belonging] to the son at the time of the loan:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:1:1.english: It is taught explicitly - that according to Rabbi Akiva, we appraise [it] based on [the property of] the damager:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:20:1.english: Relating to his son - On behalf of his son:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:21:1.hebrew: דברי הכל לא משתעבד - חדא, דערב בעלמא הוא, ועוד, לאו מידי חסרה, שלא הוציאה כלום משלה:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:21:1.english: Everyone agrees [that he] does not become obligated - First, because he is merely a guarantor, and furthermore, she has not lost anything, for she did not spend anything of her own:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:2:1.hebrew: ורבי שמעון היא - מתני' דקתני במידי דאורייתא "מפני תיקון העולם", רבי שמעון שהיה תלמיד של רבי עקיבא אמרה:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:2:1.english: And it is [authored by] Rabbi Shimon - The Mishnah, which teaches regarding a matter of Torah law "for the betterment of the world" — Rabbi Shimon, who was a disciple of Rabbi Akiva, stated it:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:2:2.hebrew: דדריש - נמי בעלמא טעמא דקרא, בבבא מציעא (דף קטו.) גבי "לא תחבול בגד אלמנה" (דברים כד), דקאמר: עשירה ממשכנין אותה:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:2:2.english: Who expounds - [he] also [expounds] elsewhere the reason [underlying] the verse, in Bava Metzia (115a) regarding [the verse], "You shall not take a widow's garment in pledge" (Deuteronomy 24:17), where he says: [From] a wealthy [widow], one may take a pledge:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:2:3.hebrew: מפני תיקון העולם - כדקתני בברייתא, שיאמר אדם: "למה אני גוזל" כו':
Rashi on Gittin 49b:2:3.english: For the betterment of the world - As the baraita teaches, [so] that a person will say: "Why should I rob," etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:2:4.hebrew: גזלן לא יהיב דמי, חמסן יהיב דמי:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:2:4.english: A robber does not pay [for what he takes], [whereas] one who seizes by force does pay:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:7:1.english: She goes out with her consent, etc. - Against her will, [her] husband divorces her:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:8:1.english: What [is] "an alternative explanation" - How is [that] a reason for a ketubah to be collected from inferior-quality land?

Rashi on Gittin 49b:8:2.hebrew: וכ"ת - כלומר, מילתא אחריתי קאמר, ולא טעמא לזיבורית הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:8:2.english: And if you would say - meaning, he is stating a different matter, and it is not a reason for [collecting from] inferior-quality land:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:8:3.hebrew: אפשר דמשהי לה - ולא יהיב לה גיטא, וכיון דלא אשהי, מדעתיה גירשה:
Rashi on Gittin 49b:8:3.english: It is possible [for him] to keep her waiting - and not give her a bill of divorce; and since he did not keep [her] waiting, he divorced her willingly:

Rashi on Gittin 49b:9:1.english: Only from orphans - such as a widow's marriage contract:

Tosafot on Gittin 49b:11:1.hebrew: משום חינא - פירש בקונטרס: שיהיו האנשים נושאים חן בעיני הנשים וינשאו להם. וקשה, דבפרק הכותב (כתובות דף פד.) תנן: ר' עקיבא אומר, ינתנו לכושל שבהם; ואיכא דמפרש בגמ' לכתובת אשה משום חינא. ולפירוש הקונטרס, לא הוה ליה למיקריה כושל, דאדרבה, האיש כושל, שצריך למצוא חן בעיני האשה! ובפרק נערה (כתובות דף נב:), וק דקדושין (דף ל:): "קחו לבניכם נשים ואת בנותיכם תתנו לאנשים" — בשלמא בנו בידו, אלא בתו מאי עביד לה? אלמא, יותר הבעל מוצא לישא אשה ממה שהאשה תמצא בעל. ולעיל נמי: יותר משהאיש רוצה לישא, אשה רוצה לינשא. ונראה כפר"ח, דפירש משום חינא: שיהו הכל קופצין עליה לישאנה, והכי איתא בהדיא בירושל' דפירקין:
Tosafot on Gittin 49b:11:1.english: For the sake of desirability - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: so that men will find favor in the eyes of women and marry them. And [this is] difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] Hakotev (Ketubot 84a) we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Akiva says, "[The funds] should be given to the weakest among them," and there is [an opinion] in the Gemara that explains [that this refers] to a woman's marriage contract, for the sake of desirability. Yet according to the explanation of the Kuntres, [the Mishnah] should not have called [her] "weak," for on the contrary, the man is the weak one, since he needs to find favor in the eyes of the woman! And in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah (Ketubot 52b) and [the first chapter] of Kiddushin (30b) [the Gemara cites]: "Take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to men" — granted [that marrying off] his son is in his power, but [with] his daughter, what can he do for her? Thus, a husband finds [it easier] to marry a wife than a woman finds a husband. And earlier as well: More than the man wants to marry, the woman wants to be married. Therefore, it appears [correct] like the explanation of Rabbeinu Ḥananel, who explained "for the sake of desirability" [as meaning]: so that everyone will jump at [the opportunity] to marry her; and so it is [stated] explicitly in the Jerusalem Talmud on our chapter:

Tosafot on Gittin 49b:12:1.hebrew: ממאן אילימא מיתמי מאי איריא כו' - הכא לא שייך לשנויי כדלעיל, "כתובת אשה איצטריכא ליה", והוא הדין כל מילי, דהא קתני "נזקין בעידית". ואית ספרים דגרסי הכי: "אילימא מיתמי, והתנן: אין נפרעין כו'", ופריך אנזקין ובעל חוב:
Tosafot on Gittin 49b:12:1.english: From whom? If we say from orphans, why specifically, etc. - Here it is not applicable to answer as above, "[Teaching the case of] a woman's marriage contract was necessary for him," and [that] the same law applies to all [other] cases — for [the baraita] teaches, "Damages [are collected] from superior-quality land." And there are texts that read thus: "If we say from orphans, but didn't we learn: One may not collect, etc.," and [the Gemara] raises the objection regarding damages and a creditor:

Tosafot on Gittin 49b:17:1.hebrew: בקבלן - פי' בקונטרס שהתפיסה בנו מטלטלין בכתובתה, והיא מסרתן לידו בתורת קבלנות, והחזירתן לבנו. וקשה, דאמרינן בגט פשוט (ב"ב דף קעד.) דהיכא דנשא ונתן ביד, אין לו למלוה על הלוה כלום. ושמא היינו שלקח המעות מיד המלוה ונתן ללוה; אף על גב דמשמע התם דבלשון תליא מילתא, שמא תרוייהו בעינן:
Tosafot on Gittin 49b:17:1.english: With an unconditional guarantor - Rashi explained that his son gave her movable property as security for her marriage contract, and she handed them over to him [i.e., to the father-in-law] as an unconditional guarantor, and she [then] returned them to his son. And this is difficult, for we say in [the chapter entitled] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 174a) that wherever [the guarantor] physically handled the transfer [lit. took and gave by hand], the lender has no [claim] against the borrower at all. And perhaps that [rule] applies [only] where he took the money from the hand of the lender and gave [it] to the borrower; even though it is implied there that the matter depends on the wording [used by the guarantor], perhaps we require both:

Tosafot on Gittin 49b:18:1.hebrew: אלא למאן דאמר אי אית ליה משתעבד כו' - והכא מיירי בדלית ליה, דאי אית ליה, נזקין אמאי בעידית, כיון שיש ממון ליתומין? דאפילו מיירי בקטנים, דלא מצי ערב לאישתעויי דינא בהדייהו, מ"מ לא היה להם לגבות כי אם מן הזיבורית, כיון דאית ליה נכסי ליתמי. ובקונטרס פי' דהכא בדלית ליה, דאי אית ליה, הא קי"ל בגט פשוט (שם דף קעג.): המלוה חבירו על ידי ערב, אין נפרעים מן הערב תחילה. וקשה, דהכא איירי בקבלן:
Tosafot on Gittin 49b:18:1.english: But according to the one who says that if he has [property] he becomes responsible, etc. - And here we are dealing with [a case] where he [the son] does not have [property]; for if he has [property], why [are] damages [collected] from superior-quality land, since the orphans have money? For even if we are dealing with minor [orphans], such that a guarantor cannot litigate with them, nevertheless they would only be able to collect from inferior-quality land, since the orphans have property. And in the Kuntres [Rashi] explained that here [we are dealing with a case] where he does not have [property]; for if he has [property], behold, we hold as established law in [the chapter entitled] Get Pashut (there, 173a): One who lends to his fellow through a guarantor may not collect from the guarantor first. And this is difficult, because here we are dealing with an unconditional guarantor [kablan]:

Tosafot on Gittin 49b:2:1.hebrew: ורבי שמעון היא דדריש טעמא דקרא - לא פליגי אלא היכא דאיכא נפקותא, כגון גבי תובל בגד אלמנה וגבי "לא ירבה לו נשים"; וה"נ, משום האי טעמא שיימינן בדמזיק:
Tosafot on Gittin 49b:2:1.english: And it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Shimon, who expounds the reason of the verse - [Rabbi Shimon and the Sages] only disagree where there is a practical difference, such as regarding taking a widow's garment as a pledge and regarding "he shall not multiply wives for himself"; and here too, because of this reason, we appraise [the property] of the one who caused the damage:

Tosafot on Gittin 49b:8:1.hebrew: וכי תימא כי היכי דכי מפיק כו' - פי' בקונטרס, משום מילתא אחריתי קאמר ולא טעמא לזיבורית הוא. ונראה לפרש דה"ק: דלא תימא על כרחך טעמא ד"יותר ממה שהאיש רוצה לישא" ליתא דחיישינן לחינא, מדלא תקינו ליה רבנן כתובה מינה אם הקניטתו עד שגירשה:
Tosafot on Gittin 49b:8:1.english: And if you would say that just as when [a man] divorces, etc. - Rashi explained [that] he says [this] regarding a different matter, and it is not a reason for [collecting from] inferior-quality land. But it appears [correct] to explain that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: [The baraita states this] so that you should not say, "Perforce, the reason that 'more than a man wants to marry [a woman, a woman wants to become married]' is not [valid], because we are concerned about [women] finding favor [with men]," [inferring this] from the fact that the Sages did not institute a marriage contract for him from her if she provoked him until he divorced her:
